chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from 'Uthman ibn 'Isa, from Zur'a, from Samaan, who said:

I asked him about a man who died leaving young and adult sons and daughters, without a will, and he had servants and slaves and debts. How should the heirs distribute that inheritance? He said, 'If a trustworthy man stands up and allocates shares for all of it, there is no harm.'

key_terms.فَلاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / it is permissible

ai.seo_question: How is an estate distributed if the deceased left no will and has minor children?
ai.summary: In the absence of a will, this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* validates the distribution of an estate by a trustworthy individual (*thiqah*) who allocates shares for all heirs, including minors, as well as assets like servants, slaves, and debts. This reflects the Shia juristic principle of *al-istihlak* or delegated distribution, ensuring that the rights of those unable to manage their affairs are preserved through a reliable agent. The inclusion of specific asset categories highlights the comprehensive nature of estate settlement in early Shia legal practice.
